prize_parts.citation: For the theoretical prediction of flat bands in twisted bilayer graphene at a magic angle and the experimental discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states in moire flat-band systems

statement.case_for: I keep B009 as my preferred single-part configuration. After the first round the case is unchanged in structure: the Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum model is a compact, analysable mechanism that predicted flat bands at a magic twist angle, and the 2018 experiments showed correlated insulators and superconductivity at that angle in a gate-tunable system. The phenomena have since been reproduced by many groups with transport, scanning probes and spectroscopy, and the twist angle is now a general control parameter across van der Waals heterostructures. The citation can be worded around what is established (flat bands, correlated insulating and superconducting states) and does not need to claim a pairing mechanism. I have changed one thing: I now treat B006 rather than B023 as my second alternative, because the round-1 exchange showed me that B006 is the strongest mature candidate, and that B023 cannot be reduced to three names without an arbitrary choice.
statement.case_against: The strongest objection is still timing. The experiments are about eight years old, the pairing mechanism is open, and Eriksson, Johansson, Kroll, Pearce and Danielsson all weigh this as a real concern. Credit is also imperfect: first author Yuan Cao and other 2018 experimentalists cannot be named under the three-person limit, and earlier twisted-bilayer band-structure theory (Lopes dos Santos, Peres, Castro Neto; Suarez Morell; Kaxiras and Santos) is left outside. The chair's count shows B006 holding four first preferences against my two, and I accept that B006 is the safer prize on maturity and clean attribution. My preference for B009 is a judgment that conceptual novelty and the prediction-to-discovery link should outweigh that margin, not a claim that the clock case is scientifically weak.

responses.point: Eriksson prefers B004 on the ground that topological insulators are confirmed across several material families for more than fifteen years, whereas twisted bilayer graphene is young and its superconductivity unexplained, and argues that the Z2 class is distinct from the 2016 prize.
responses.response: I accept the maturity point, and it is the best argument against my own ballot. I also accept that the Z2 invariant is a different symmetry-protected class from the Thouless-Haldane-Kosterlitz subject matter, so I no longer rest my doubts on repetition. My remaining difficulty with B004 is the credit chain. You concede yourself that Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang proposed the HgTe route that Molenkamp realised, that Zhang cannot be recognised, and that the three-dimensional work (Fu, Kane, Mele, Moore, Balents, Hasan) interlocks with it. A trio of Kane, Mele and Molenkamp is defensible but the boundary is a convention. For B009 the boundary is a two-author 2011 paper, plus the first experiment. That is why I keep B009 first and B004 as my alternative. I would not oppose B004 if the committee wants the more settled condensed-matter prize.

responses.point: Lindroth argues that the optical lattice clock is a distinct concept (magic wavelength, many atoms interrogated at once), not a refinement of the 2005 or 2012 prizes, and that the citation should name the invention and its realisation. She also asks, if a moire prize is chosen, that the citation state what is established and not the mechanism.
responses.response: Her answer to the overlap objection persuades me more than I expected. The magic-wavelength condition is a clean mechanism: it removes the lattice light shift so that many atoms can be held without perturbing the transition. That is the kind of simple, general idea I value, and it is distinct from both a frequency comb and a single trapped ion. I therefore withdraw the suggestion in round 1 that a clock prize would read mainly as a precision record, and I now treat B006 as a first-rate alternative rather than a safe one. I take her request about wording seriously, and my citation says phenomena, not pairing mechanism. Where we still differ is on how a prize is weighed: I would give more weight to a newly opened regime of correlated matter than to a better ruler, but I recognise that the committee majority does not read it that way.

responses.point: Johansson moved from B015 to B006 after the openings, considers the Katori idea and the Ye-group record not trivially balanced, and says B023 is not ready as a three-name prize because he and I propose different trios (Bloch, Greiner, Zoller versus Bloch, Cirac, Zoller).
responses.response: His point on B023 is correct and I concede it. My own trio differs from his and Lindroth's, and with five credited names and no obvious three, any choice leaves out decisive theory or experiment. That is why I have dropped B023 from my alternatives in favour of B006. On B006 I agree that the Katori-versus-Ye weighting is not settled by a citation alone. If the committee goes there, the safest wording names the magic-wavelength lattice concept and its realisation at the 10^-18 level, which keeps the Yb, Sr and Al+ groups from being read as excluded. I still disagree that the open pairing mechanism makes B009 premature in the way he suggests: the existence of the flat-band phases is reproduced, and the prize tradition has accepted robust phenomena with unresolved microscopic explanations.

responses.point: Olsson prefers B009 with the same trio, accepts that the pairing mechanism, the omitted first author and the age of the field are weaknesses, and holds B006 as her alternative.
responses.response: We agree on the trio and on the wording around observed phenomena. I would add one point to the chair's open question on the credit boundary. I would keep Bistritzer rather than drop to two names, because the continuum model is the half of the story that makes the magic angle understandable, and Eriksson's own preference for MacDonald and Jarillo-Herrero alone would weaken the theory half of the citation. I accept that Yuan Cao and the other 2018 experimentalists cannot be named within three people and that we should say so openly. Unlike you I have no stake in B012, but I note that your recusal there does not affect B009 or B006.

responses.point: Pearce, as chair, moved from B043 to B006 on the argument that seven members ranked it and that performance is quantified and reproduced in several laboratories, and holds B043 and B004 as alternatives.
responses.response: I agree with the reproducibility argument for B006, and I accept that it differs from my own case in that the performance metric is unambiguous. I do not think the breadth of ranking alone settles the choice, since the committee is supposed to weigh the scientific case, but here the breadth is backed by reasons. On B043 I stay where I was: a diffuse flux seen independently is solid, but credit among Halzen, Spiering and the AMANDA and Baikal precursors is not resolved with two names, and TXS 0506+056 is a single-source statement of modest significance. I would also want expert reports on 2001-03 priority for B006 and on the first-author question for B009 before anyone relies on memory of the literature, including mine.

uncertainties: Whether the open superconducting mechanism and the age of the field (about eight years) make B009 premature compared with the clock and topological-insulator prizes.

Whether the credit for the 2018 experiments should be reconsidered given that Yuan Cao and other experimentalists cannot be named, and whether Bistritzer should stay beside MacDonald and Jarillo-Herrero.
Whether an expert report would show earlier twisted-bilayer theory (Lopes dos Santos, Peres, Castro Neto; Suarez Morell; Kaxiras and Santos) to be decisive for the magic-angle prediction.

For B006, whether Katori and Ye are the right pair given Ludlow, Lemonde, Hinkley and Bloom, and whether the 2001-03 priority record supports Katori; I have not verified this and rely on recollection.
Whether the committee should prefer the clock prize because of its maturity even though a majority of its supporters name the overlap with the 2005 and 2012 prizes as a weakness.
statement.conflict_note: No change to my disclosure. I have no known collaboration or institutional tie to MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero, Bistritzer, Katori, Ye, Kane, Mele or Molenkamp. I share the Gothenburg physics environment with Johansson (Chalmers) and Olsson (Chalmers), who have disclosed ties to B015 and B012, neither of which is in my configuration. My own work on random matrices and statistical models of complex systems is adjacent to, but not part of, moire quantum matter. I see no reason to recuse myself from any shortlisted ballot.
